source: Vacation days and raises: national minimums and typical practice (US BLS, UK gov.uk, Japan and Korea labour law), historical practice for older eras; projects written for Prospero's Companion 2026-10-13.

us.note: No legal minimum; about 11 paid days in the first years (BLS).

uk.note: 28 days statutory including bank holidays; 25 plus bank holidays is usual.

japan.note: 10 days by law after six months, few taken; raises in April after shunto.

south-korea.note: 15 days by law after a year.

us-1920s.note: A paid week was a perk for office workers; many had none.

us-1880s.note: No paid holidays; a better wage now and then.

uk-victorian.note: Bank holidays from 1871, no paid leave; wages reviewed at Lady Day.

medieval-england.note: Feast days only; wages agreed at Michaelmas.
